title: The iPSC-derived pulmonary epithilial cells in micro-patterned culture plate [CUT&Tag]
overall_design: Human iPSC-derived lung progenitor cells were seeded onto micro-patterned plates and cultured in "DCIK+3i" (CHIR99021, SB431542 and Y27632) medium for 7 days to induce alveolar organoids involving alveolar type 2 cells in the DCIK+3i medium. Thereafter, the alveolar organoids were cultured in the following three conditions for 7 days: "DCIK+3i" to maintain alveolar type 2 cells, "DCI+LATS(LATS-IN-1)" to induce alveolar type 1 cells, or "PAL" to induce alveolar transitional state cells (iATCs), respectively. The organoids in each condition were dissociated using Accutase and subjected to CUT&TAG analysis.
type: Genome binding/occupancy profiling by high throughput sequencing

title: iATCs_CUT1_H3K27ac
characteristics_ch1: cell type: iPSC-derived alveolar epithelial cells
growth_protocol_ch1: The MACS-isolated iPSC-derived lung progenitor cells (LPs) were seeded in the 24-well micro-patterned plates for "2.5-dimensional culture" (Tosoh Co., Ltd.) with multiple round shaped cell-attachment areas in 100 μm diameter pre-coated with 0.5 ug/cm2 of iMatrix-511 silk (TaKaRa bio, 892021) at the cell densities 1x10^5 cells/well. These cells were cultured in "DCIK+3i" (CHIR99021, SB431542, and Y27632) medium for 7 days to induce AT2 cells, followed by an additional 7-day maintenance with DCIK+3i medium to induce AT2 cells, DCI+LATS medium to induce AT1 cells, or PAL medium to induce iATCs, respectively.
extract_protocol_ch1: For the isolation of iAT2 and iAT1 cells, the cells cultured on micro-patterned plates were first stained with Hoechst-33342 for 30 minutes at 37°C, followed by incubation with Accutase at 37°C for 20 minutes and dissociation by gentle pipetting. For the isolation of iATCs, the cells were incubated with Accutase, gently dissociated by pipetting, and stained with an APC-conjugated anti-human CD54 antibody for 20 minutes at 4°C. Each positive cell population was then sorted using fluorescence-activated cell sorting.

To make the CUT&Tag libraries, the dissociated cells were washed with PBS supplemented with 1X Protease Inhibitor (Roche, # 11873580001), and subsequently washed with wash buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.25 mM spermidine, 1X Protease Inhibitor (Roche, # 11873580001)). Then, we resuspended 50,000 cells in 500 µl of the wash buffer supplemented with 5 mM sodium butyrate. We added 2 µl of the concanavalin A-conjugated magnetic beads to the cell suspension. Next, after magnetic separation of the beads and removal of the supernatant, we resuspended the beads in 50 µL of ice-cold wash buffer, supplemented with 5 mM sodium butyrate, 0.05% digitonin, 2 mM EDTA, and 0.1% BSA together with 0.5 µl primary antibody against H3K27Ac (MAB Institute, #MABI0309) or H3 (MAB Institute, #MABI0301). After rotating incubation at room temperature for 3 hours, the buffer containing the primary antibody was replaced with 100 µl of ice-cold wash buffer, supplemented with 5 mM sodium butyrate, 0.05% digitonin, together with 1 µl secondary rabbit anti-mouse IgG antibody (Abcam, #ab46540), and was incubated at 4 °C for overnight. After washing the beads with Dig-300 buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 300 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM spermidine, 0.01% digitonin, 1X Protease Inhibitor (Roche, # 11873580001), 5 mM sodium butyrate) twice, we applied 100 µl of the Dig-300 buffer containing 3.6 femtomol pA-Tn5 transposome and incubated the mixture for 1 hour at room temperature. After washing the beads with the Dig-300 buffer twice, we resuspended the beads in 50 µl of the Dig-300 buffer supplemented with 10 mM MgCl2 and incubated them at 37 °C for 1 hour. We then removed the supernatant and resuspended the beads in 20 µl of 10 mM TAPS buffer (pH 8.5) together with 0.5 µl thermolabile proteinase K (NEB, #P8111S), and incubated the mixture at 37 °C for 30 minutes, followed by incubation at 55 °C for 20 minutes to inactivate the proteinase. We directly performed PCR-amplification of the library from the tube after adding the reaction mixture (KAPA BIOSYSTEMS, #KK2602) using index primers. The amplified libraries were purified with 1.3 volumes of AMPure XP beads.
data_processing: We used “DNA-mapping” in snakePipes (v2.7.3) (PMID: 31134269) to trim adapter sequences with fastp (v0.23.2) (PMID: 38868435) and to subsequently map the remaining sequences with bowtie2 (v2.4.5) (PMID: 22388286) against the reference sequence created from the human T2T-CHM13v2.0 genome assembly without Y chromosome together with the complete genome sequence of Escherichia coli strain BL21 (GenBank: CP010816.1) and the 3XFlag-pA-Tn5-Fl plasmid sequence (Addgene, #124601).

We obtained a bam file only with properly-paired alignments mapped to the human chromosomes 1 to 22 and X with the MAPQ score greater than or equal to 10 using samtools view command (v1.15.1) (PMID: 19505943) with the option “-f 2 -F 256 -x XA -q 10.
We further created bigwig tracks from the bam files using “bamCoverage” in deeptools (v3.5.1) (PMID: 27079975) with the option “--binSize 25 --effectiveGenomeSize 3054815472 --normalizeUsing CPM.
We called peaks with MACS2 callpeak (v2.2.7.1) (PMID: 18798982) with the option “-f BAM -g hs --nomodel” using the snakemake wrapper v2.1.0 in a snakemake workflow (PMID: 22908215).
Assembly: Human T2T-CHM13v2.0
Supplementary files format and content: BigWig files include signal intensity values across the genome for each sample
Library strategy: CUT&Tag

data_processing: We used “DNA-mapping” in snakePipes (v2.7.3) (PMID: 31134269) to trim adapter sequences with fastp (v0.23.2) (PMID: 38868435) and to subsequently map the remaining sequences with bowtie2 (v2.4.5) (PMID: 22388286) against the reference sequence created from the human T2T-CHM13v2.0 genome assembly without Y chromosome together with the complete genome sequence of Escherichia coli strain BL21 (GenBank: CP010816.1) and the 3XFlag-pA-Tn5-Fl plasmid sequence (Addgene, #124601).

We obtained a bam file only with properly-paired alignments mapped to the human chromosomes 1 to 22 and X with the MAPQ score greater than or equal to 10 using samtools view command (v1.15.1) (PMID: 19505943) with the option “-f 2 -F 256 -x XA -q 10.
We further created bigwig tracks from the bam files using “bamCoverage” in deeptools (v3.5.1) (PMID: 27079975) with the option “--binSize 25 --effectiveGenomeSize 3054815472 --normalizeUsing CPM.
We called peaks with MACS2 callpeak (v2.2.7.1) (PMID: 18798982) with the option “-f BAM -g hs --nomodel” using the snakemake wrapper v2.1.0 in a snakemake workflow (PMID: 22908215).
Assembly: Human T2T-CHM13v2.0
Supplementary files format and content: BigWig files include signal intensity values across the genome for each sample
Library strategy: CUT&Tag
